excerpt: Fall 2026 DVC-3342-ATruth-Telling 101 Learn how New York's leading newsrooms turn raw data into compelling journalism What this is Data science on deadline In this hands-on introduction to data journalism, students will learn how to blend cutting-edge statistical analysis with time-tested reporting techniques. You will practice the fundamental skills of the craft by working through the full arc of data-driven stories, together in class and then on your own. By the end of the six-week course, you will be ready to pitch a professional editor. “To cope with the acceleration of social change in today's world, journalism must become social science in a hurry.” Philip Meyer What we'll cover Fundamental skills You'll get multiple rounds of practice applying the key techniques common to every data story. Locating data that can provide the answers Preparing raw data for rigorous analysis Interviewing data to develop meaningful findings Verifying your findings in the real world Ensuring subjects have an opportunity to respond Visiting experts Meet our guest speakers Three of the city's best data reporters will join our class to share how they turn data into impactful journalism. Faculty Meet your instructor Each class will be led in person by a working professional. Ben Welsh News Applications Editor, Reuters I am a reporter, editor and computer programmer with more than 20 years of journalism experience. You contact me at b@palewi.re. Documentation Classroom scripts All of the materials we cover will be made available after class. Social science in a hurry October 5, 2026
